newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent bounces through $19 on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent bounces through $19 on short-covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures bounced through $19 on short-covering in late morning trade ahead of the NYMEX opening, but gas oil lagged the crude gains, remaining stuck in a narrow, 25-cent range, traders said.
By 1135 GMT the October Brent contract stood at the session high of $19.05 a barrel, up 12 cents as short-covering against perceptions that a firmer NYMEX opening will lift the market.
Oct Brent was sold lower in early trade with little buying interest seen until key technical support came in around $18.93.
Gas oil hardly moved. Holding a narrow range around $170.75 and $170.50 the September contract was $1 up at $170.50 a tonne.

The uptrends for NYMEX crude and product futures remain intact for the time being, with technical indicators pointing out a slow route to higher ground, but the impetus is slowing with gasoline, the recent market leader, running out of steam.

"Gasoline virtually negated the reverse head and shoulders formation that some participants were looking towards on Monday, but the recovery before the close may have given the bulls mild encouragement." Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said.
"Whether the market can take off again depends largely on a particular fundamental influence tone, the APIs. The uptrend in this market is still holding, but only just," he said.
